name: Cluster
description: Neo4j Enterprise HA cluster lifecycle: the Neo4jEnterpriseCluster CRD, rolling upgrades, scale-down drains, storage expansion, topology scheduling, split-brain detection, and live diagnostics.

name: Standalone
description: Single-node Neo4j Enterprise deployments (dev/test/low-availability) via the Neo4jEnterpriseStandalone CRD, sharing most cluster infrastructure with replicas=1.

name: Database Lifecycle
description: In-cluster database lifecycle CRDs: Neo4jDatabase, Neo4jDatabaseAlias, Neo4jShardedDatabase (property sharding), Neo4jReplicaDatabase and Neo4jReplicaPromotion (cross-cluster replication / DR failover).

name: Backup & Restore
description: Neo4jBackup / Neo4jRestore: Job-per-CR backups (never a long-running backup pod), point-in-time recovery, and cluster-vs-standalone restore engines.

name: Users, Roles & ABAC
description: Identity and access management: Neo4jUser, Neo4jRole, Neo4jRoleBinding (privileges live only on Neo4jRole), and Neo4jAuthRule (attribute-based access control mapping OIDC claims to roles).

name: Plugins
description: Neo4jPlugin: installs and configures APOC, Graph Data Science, Bloom, GenAI, n10s, and GraphQL plugins with automatic security configuration.

name: Aura Instance Lifecycle
description: Neo4j Aura cloud instance lifecycle via the Aura API: AuraProviderConfig, AuraInstance, AuraSnapshot, AuraRestore, AuraCustomerManagedKey, AuraIPFilter.

name: Aura Databases
description: Per-database lifecycle on a multi-database Aura instance: AuraDatabase, AuraDatabaseBackup, AuraDatabaseRestore (all Aura API v2beta1, beta/best-effort).

name: Aura Console RBAC
description: Aura CONSOLE identity (who can use the Aura console/projects, not in-database Neo4j users): AuraOrganizationMember, AuraProjectMember, AuraInvite.

name: Platform
description: Cross-cutting operator plumbing shared by every CRD: manager bootstrap and health/metrics endpoints, the Neo4j Bolt client, inline spec validators (never an admission webhook), clusterRef/backupRef resolvers, and K8s resource builders.

name: CLI
description: kubectl-neo4j, the customer-facing kubectl plugin shipped on the operator's own release tag. It reuses the operator's packages rather than restating their rules: validation from internal/validation, workload selectors and cloud-credential contracts from internal/resources. It may create and read custom resources and read Kubernetes state, and never executes Cypher or neo4j-admin for a mutating operation.
